polar.payouts.caveat: Payouts run on Stripe Connect Express; individuals need Stripe Express to support the 'individual' business type in your country (check per Polar's FAQ).

Also excluded: Crimea, DPR, LPR, individual nationals of Cuba, SDN-listed persons, and 'any other country or region restricted by law (this changes occasionally)'. Hand-curated from the help article (not an automated collector).

whop.payouts.caveat: Payout methods (bank, PayPal, crypto) vary by country and are shown in your Whop balance screen.

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes. Guatemalan banks offer US-dollar accounts, a common product for people who invoice in USD or receive remittances. The initial deposit must be in USD (cash, an international cheque or a transfer from another USD account). Banks typically ask for a DPI or passport, an active NIT and proof of address; minimum deposits vary by bank (Living in Guatemala).

L7_incentives.question: Legal incentives / tax holidays / special zones relevant to small digital businesses
L7_incentives.answer: Régimen de Pequeño Contribuyente: a flat 5% of gross income (no VAT credit), declared monthly. Decreto 31-2024 raised the annual income ceiling from Q150,000 to 125 monthly minimum wages: Q465,381.25 in 2025 and Q500,285 in 2026. If you exceed the ceiling, you must move to the general regime (12% VAT with input credit) (Living in Guatemala).

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) Client payments by PayPal (on PayPal's Payouts list as 'Send, receive, and withdraw'). (6) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
